description: From the fz-k22.13 audit. JobSet (insertion-ordered subscriber/waiter set, deps.rs:36-59) does remove via members.remove (O(1)) + order.retain (O(n) over the whole per-fact subscriber list), called from replace_reads/replace_waits on EVERY job re-run, once per previously-subscribed fact. No measurable delta on current fixtures (quicksort 0.022s vs 0.026s), but a fact with large subscriber fan-out could hit O(n^2). Options if it ever profiles hot: index-assisted swap-remove, or tombstone+compact. At minimum add a comment in deps.rs acknowledging the tradeoff vs Agenda (VecDeque pop_front never needs retain -- different access pattern, the "same idiom" claim is directional not literal).

comments.text:
SUPERSEDED by fz-kdt.7 under the fz-kdt re-baseline epic.

The type this ticket names, JobSet, no longer exists -- fz-f98.19 generalized it into OrderedSet<T> and widened its use to the fact-output paths as well, because a job's emission order turned out to be load-bearing for reproducibility. The O(n) retain concern carries over verbatim and now covers MORE paths, so the ticket is still valid; it just cannot be found by its old name. Restated with current names in fz-kdt.7, including the new constraint that swap-remove is no longer an option because insertion order is load-bearing. Work continues there.

title: compiler2 deps.rs JobSet::remove is O(n) retain in the hottest fixpoint loop -- watch item / profile before large-fanout workloads
